title: 10-yield ceiling in select-closed test is underdocumented
description: events_coalescing_task_exits_via_select_closed_arm uses 10 yield_now() calls after drop(resp) and asserts receiver_count()==0. In the single-threaded current_thread runtime, 1 yield suffices: drop(resp) wakes the task synchronously, the first yield gives it control, select\! closed() fires, task exits, rx dropped, receiver_count()==0. The comment says 'yield several times to let the select\! closed() arm fire' but does not explain why 10 was chosen or what the theoretical minimum is. A future reader cannot tell whether 10 is a measured margin, cargo-culted from the subscribe loop, or a guess. A one-line comment stating '1 is the theoretical minimum; 10 provides scheduler headroom' would prevent future confusion.
